## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two sets
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},\qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}
  \]
  generate \(J_v\subseteq H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\); each has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [source-backed] The paper conjectures that both sets are minimal and reports computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [source-backed] The paper applies its graded proposition with \(\Lambda\) the graded ring of symmetric functions over \(\mathbb Z\), \(M=J_v\), and explicitly leaves unresolved whether \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(N\) generators or is \(\mathbb Z^N\). [source-2, lines 1517-1552]
- [proved] **Indexed graded Nakayama.** Let \(R\) be commutative unital, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{e\ge0}\Lambda_e\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra with \(\Lambda_0=R\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge d_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For any indexed homogeneous family \((m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\), it generates \(M\) iff \((\bar m_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}\) spans \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Indeed, the forward direction is immediate. Conversely, induct on \(d\). For \(x\in M_d\), gradedness gives
  \[
  x-\sum_{\alpha\in F,\ \deg m_\alpha=d}r_\alpha m_\alpha\in(\Lambda_+M)_d
  =\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e},
  \]
  for a finite \(F\subset A\). Every latter module factor has degree \(<d\), hence belongs to the generated submodule by induction.
- [proved] Under the hypotheses above, the family \((m_\alpha)\) is inclusion-minimal precisely when \((\bar m_\alpha)\) is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning family of \(Q\): apply indexed graded Nakayama to every subfamily obtained by deleting one index.
- [proved] If \(A=\Lambda/I\), \(J\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq J\), then \(S\) generates \(J\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(J\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. Thus the preceding criterion applies to \(J_v\).
- [proved] An exact sufficient hypothesis for either displayed \(N\)-element Schur family to be irredundant is
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}\!\left(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\right)=N.
  \]
  It spans the quotient by graded Nakayama; deletion would give a spanning family of \(N-1\) elements, contradicting the hypothesis.
- [proved] A stronger sufficient hypothesis is
  \[
  J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N.
  \]
  An \(N\)-element spanning family of \(\mathbb Z^N\) cannot remain spanning after a deletion, since \(\mathbb Z^{N-1}\) cannot surject onto \(\mathbb Z^N\).
- [proved] **Free-summand irredundance construction.** If \(R\ne0\), \(Q=R^d\oplus T\), and \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\) is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(T\), then
  \[
  \{(e_\ell,0):1\le\ell\le d\}\ \cup\ \{(0,t_j):1\le j\le k\}
  \]
  is an inclusion-minimal spanning family of \(Q\). Coordinate projections witness necessity of the first \(d\) elements, and \(Q\to T\) witnesses necessity of the others.
- [proved] **CRT-aligned construction.** Let \(n_1,\ldots,n_k>1\) be pairwise coprime, \(M=\prod_i n_i\), and \(T=\mathbb Z/M\). Choose \(c_i\) with \(c_i(M/n_i)\equiv1\pmod {n_i}\), and put \(\epsilon_i=c_iM/n_i\bmod M\). Under
  \[
  T\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^k\mathbb Z/n_i,
  \]
  \(\epsilon_i\) is the \(i\)-th coordinate unit. Hence \(\{\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_k\}\) is inclusion-minimal spanning, while \(\{1\}\) is also inclusion-minimal spanning.
- [proved] Claim 9 is correct: in \(\mathbb Z/6\), \(\{1\}\) generates, while \(\{2,3\}\) generates because \(1=2\cdot2-3\), and neither singleton \(\{2\}\) nor \(\{3\}\) generates. Thus both are inclusion-minimal, of cardinalities \(1\) and \(2\). More generally, adjoining the free summand \(\mathbb Z^d\) to the CRT construction gives irredundant spanning families of \(\mathbb Z^d\oplus\mathbb Z/M\) of sizes \(d+1\) and \(d+k\).
- [conjectural] No supplied evidence proves \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)=\binom{a+b}{a}\), torsion-freeness of this quotient, or the source’s stronger \(\mathbb Z^N\) formulation; consequently the minimality conjecture for \(J_v\) remains unresolved.

## Strategy
Apply indexed graded Nakayama to either Schur family, using the quotient \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\). Prove minimality from either the generator-number condition \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\), or from explicit quotient witnesses such as a free-coordinate projection.

## Gaps
No presentation, Smith normal form, prime-field lower bound, or free-summand/CRT decomposition of the actual quotient \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) is supplied. The abstract constructions therefore do not establish the needed hypothesis for \(J_v\).

## Next
Construct an integral presentation of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) and determine its generator number, including all torsion primes.
